design.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study with a 6-month active treatment period; 123 patients randomized 1:1 to edaravone or placebo in the double-blind portion.

citations.quote: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, comparative, with 6-month active treatment period
It is a multicenter study with 123 patients randomized 1:1 to active or placebo in the double-blind portion.

population.text: ALS patients categorized as Definite or Probable ALS by El Escorial revised Airlie House criteria, Japan ALS severity Grade 1 or 2, with onset within 2 years (Definite or Probable/EESP/2y population).

citations.quote: Based upon the findings in Study MCI186-16, Study MCI186-19 was prospectively designed to enroll the Definite or Probable/EESP/2y ALS population.

(1) Patients who are categorized as either “Definite ALS” or “Probable ALS” in the El Escorial revised Airlie House diagnostic criteria(2) Patients at Grade 1 or 2 in the Japan ALS severity classification

endpoint.text: Change from Baseline (in Cycle 1) to the end of Cycle 6 (24 weeks) in the Revised ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) score.

citations.quote: ALSFRS-R score change from “baseline in Cycle 1” to “the end of Cycle 6 or discontinuation” was analyzed by using the factors in a dynamic allocation as covariates to perform treatment group comparisons.
Figure 11 shows estimated treatment differences in ALSFRS-R change at the end of Cycle 6 (24 weeks) within individual sites in study 19.

n.text: 137 patients in the double-blind phase safety analysis set (placebo n=68, edaravone n=69); 123 patients in the active phase (P-E n=58, E-E n=65).

P-E group: placebo group in double-blind phase of MCI186-19 followed by edaravone group in active phase of MCI186-19

result.text: Least-squares mean difference in ALSFRS-R change (edaravone – placebo) of 2.49 ± 0.76 (95% CI 0.99 to 3.98), P = 0.0013.

citations.quote: The Least Square Mean \pm Standard Error (SE) of the difference between the groups \pm SE (edaravone group – placebo group) and the 95% confidence interval of this mean was 2.49 \pm 0.76 (0.99 to 3.98).

The primary endpoint in Study 19, the difference between treatment groups in the change from Baseline on the ALSFRS-R analyzed with clinically relevant covariates, was statistically significant with P = 0.0013.

indication.text: RADICAVA is indicated for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

citations.quote: RADICAVA is indicated for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

target_moa.text: Mechanism of action in ALS is unknown; edaravone is thought to be a free radical scavenger proposed to counter oxidative damage hypothesized to occur in the nervous system of ALS patients.

citations.quote: The mechanism by which RADICAVA exerts its therapeutic effect in patients with ALS is unknown.
Edaravone is thought to be a free radical scavenger with a proposed mechanism of countering oxidative damage hypothesized to occur in the nervous system of patients with ALS.
Figure 1 Structure of 5-Methyl-2-phenyl-2,4-dihydro-3H-pyrazol-3-one ("edaravone")

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and greater than placebo) were contusion (15% vs 9%), gait disturbance (13% vs 9%), and headache (10% vs 6%). Serious concerns include hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions and sulfite allergic reactions (sodium bisulfite content).

citations.quote:
Contusion	15	9
Gait disturbance	13	9
Headache	10	6
Dermatitis	8	5
Eczema	7	4
Respiratory failure, respiratory disorder, hypoxia	6	4
Glycosuria	4	2
Tinea infection	4	2

Hypersensitivity reactions (redness, wheals, and erythema multiforme) and cases of anaphylaxis (urticaria, decreased blood pressure, and dyspnea) have been reported in spontaneous postmarketing reports with RADICAVA.
RADICAVA contains sodium bisulfite, a sulfite that may cause allergic type reactions, including anaphylactic symptoms and life-threatening or less severe asthmatic episodes in susceptible people.

citations.quote: No advisory committee meeting was convened to discuss this application. An advisory committee meeting was not deemed necessary to judge whether the data were adequate to establish the efficacy or safety of edaravone for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

requirement.text: 3208-5: A randomized, double-blind, controlled trial of edaravone in ALS patients (Definite or Probable), randomized 1:1:1 to the approved 60 mg regimen, 60 mg with a daily/near-daily regimen, or 120 mg with a daily/near-daily regimen; primary endpoint change in ALSFRS-R over a study duration of at least 24 weeks.

citations.quote: 3208-5 Conduct a randomized, double-blind, controlled trial of edaravone in patients with ALS (definite or probable, according to ALS El Escorial Revised Airlie House criteria). Patients should be randomized (1:1:1) to the approved dosing regimen and dosage of edaravone (60 mg), the approved dosage of edaravone (60mg) with a daily or near-daily dosing regimen, or to a dosage of 120 mg of edaravone (a dosage even higher would be desirable if supported by safety data), with a daily or near-daily dosing regimen.
The primary efficacy endpoint will be the change in the revised ALS functional rating scale score (ALSFRS-R) from baseline to the end of the study. The study duration will be at least 24 weeks.

No accelerated approval, breakthrough, or priority review designations applied.
